EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Tensions in the Strait of Hormuz have critically escalated following an Iranian drone attack on a Singapore-flagged cargo vessel, prompting the UN International Maritime Organization to suspend ship escort operations in the area. Concurrently, Israeli officials have declared an intent to maintain indefinite military presence in "security zones" in Lebanon, Syria, and Gaza, further raising regional instability.

IRAN
Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) attacked a Singapore-flagged cargo vessel, the *Ever Lovely* or *Ever Lonely*, in the Strait of Hormuz with a drone near the coast of Oman, causing damage to the ship's bridge but no casualties. The attack occurred hours after Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) warned ships against using non-Iranian-approved routes and declared that vessels outside designated frameworks would not receive safety guarantees or insurance. Iran has proposed charging fees for security, safety, and environmental services in the Strait, estimating potential annual revenue of up to $40 billion, a plan rejected by the US and Oman. The UN International Maritime Organization (IMO) has temporarily suspended its ship escort and evacuation operations in the Strait of Hormuz following the attack.

Mohammad-Baqer Zolghadr, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, and IRGC Quds Force Commander Esmail Qaani were seen together in a rare public image during an Ashura mourning ceremony. Qaani has warned Israel to withdraw from southern Lebanon voluntarily or face defeat. Iran's lead negotiator, Mohammad-Baqer Qalibaf, dismissed US claims that Iran's unfrozen assets would be used to purchase US agricultural products, stating that the only harvest from decades of US actions is "mistrust." US Vice President JD Vance reported an agreement to establish a direct military communication channel between the IRGC and US CENTCOM in Doha to de-escalate tensions. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the reopening of Canadian embassies in Iran and Venezuela, emphasizing that diplomatic presence does not signify policy endorsement. Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni stated Italy has not participated in any war against Iran, providing only technical and logistical support. Russia has expressed readiness to participate in the UN Security Council resolution process once a final agreement between Iran and the US is reached.

ISRAEL
An Israeli reserve soldier, Master Sgt. (res.) Basil Sweid, 32, a truck driver from Peki'in, was killed last night in an "operational accident" when his refueling truck overturned in the Rab al-Thalathine area of southern Lebanon. A combat soldier was moderately injured in the same incident. Additionally, a fighting officer was moderately injured, and another officer and two soldiers were lightly injured in an encounter with a militant in the Ya'aroun area of southern Lebanon.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz affirmed that Israeli forces would remain indefinitely in "security zones" in Lebanon, Syria, and the Gaza Strip to protect Israeli residents and communities from "jihadist elements," vowing no compromise on supreme security interests or withdrawal. Netanyahu also reiterated that Iran would not acquire nuclear weapons under his leadership. President Isaac Herzog's helicopter made an emergency landing at Palmachim Airbase after a bird strike during a flight from Jerusalem; no injuries or damage were reported. Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar plans to bring a resolution to the government on Sunday to officially recognize the Armenian Genocide, a move that would be seen as a direct challenge to Turkey. IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir stressed the need for "every male and female combat soldier and every male and female commander," seeking balance between diverse populations and military cohesion amid debates on integrating women into tank units. Germany and Israel conducted a joint naval exercise off the coast of Haifa.

GAZA & WEST BANK
The IDF announced the killing of Adam Muhammad Ibrahim Abu Hadid, a commander in Palestinian Islamic Jihad's (PIJ) "weapon production array," in a strike in Khan Younis on Tuesday. Abu Hadid was responsible for manufacturing and supplying weapons to PIJ's military wing and posed an "immediate threat" to IDF troops. Israeli leaders, including Prime Minister Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz, stated that the IDF would remain in "security zones" in the Gaza Strip for an indefinite period.

LEBANON
The IDF reported striking and killing six Hezbollah operatives in southern Lebanon who posed a threat to Israeli troops. In one incident in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, Golani Brigade troops spotted five operatives, and in another near the Ali Taher ridge, Commando Brigade troops spotted an armed gunman. The IDF is continuing operations at the Ali Taher ridge, where 30 Hezbollah operatives are reportedly holed up in an underground complex, with the IDF vowing not to allow them to exit.

A US official told Reuters that Israel had withdrawn from parts of the security zone in southern Lebanon, with the Lebanese army expected to deploy there. However, both IDF sources and Lebanese media denied any Israeli withdrawal, stating no instructions from the political leadership had been received. Simultaneously, heavy Israeli airstrikes were reported in Nabatieh al-Fawqa, Al-Mansouri, and Beit Yahoun. Hezbollah member of parliament warned the Lebanese government against making any concessions to Israel, emphasizing that nothing would pass in Lebanon without Hezbollah's agreement. Quds Force Commander Esmail Qaani threatened Israel with a "humiliating retreat" if it did not voluntarily withdraw from Lebanon. Italy and France announced plans to form a new coalition to support Lebanon after the UNIFIL mandate expires at year's end. Discussions between Lebanese and American delegations and Israel on security arrangements in "pilot areas" reportedly faced a deadlock, with Israel insisting on Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) presence north and south of the Litani River, which Lebanon rejects.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Clashes between Jaulani gangs, reportedly due to internal disputes, resulted in homes and cars being burned and several deaths in Al-Ghazlaniya, rural Damascus. In Iraq, an explosion occurred at a Hashd al-Sha'abi ammunition depot in Camp Al-Mansouriya in Diyala province. Initial reports from the Iraqi Ministry of Defense indicated no casualties, but later, the 24th Brigade of Hashd al-Sha'abi denied any explosion or fire at their facilities in the camp, stating operations were normal. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz reiterated that Israeli forces would remain indefinitely in "security zones" in Syria.

GULF STATES
A Wall Street Journal investigation revealed that the damage to the US Navy's Fifth Fleet headquarters, satellite communication facilities, warehouses, and residential buildings at Naval Support Activity Bahrain from Iranian attacks between late February and June was significantly greater than previously reported. Rebuilding costs are estimated at $400 million, with total costs expected to be much higher, prompting the Pentagon to reconsider its force posture, including potential reductions in Kuwait and Saudi Arabia, moving capabilities westward, and even transferring some to Israel in the future. The US and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) issued a joint statement welcoming the US-Iran memorandum of understanding but stressed the importance of confronting Iranian threats, including missiles, drones, and proxy support, to achieve regional peace. They also emphasized the necessity of freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and stated that any trade with Iran is conditional on its adherence to the MoU. Iraq is reportedly considering withdrawing from OPEC if its oil production quota is not substantially increased, citing a severe financial crisis exacerbated by the war in Iran impacting its oil exports. Saudi security forces reportedly kidnapped an Iraqi citizen from Basra during Umrah for posting photos of destroyed graves in Al-Baqi on social media. Oman's Foreign Minister Badr Al Busaidi stated that future arrangements for the Strait of Hormuz would not include transit fees, placing Oman in a difficult position between US demands for free passage and Iranian pressure for control.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Iranian Drone Attack in Hormuz:** An Iranian drone attacked a Singapore-flagged cargo vessel (*Ever Lovely/Lonely*) in the Strait of Hormuz near Oman, causing bridge damage.
2.  **IMO Suspends Hormuz Operations:** The UN International Maritime Organization (IMO) temporarily suspended its ship escort and evacuation operations in the Strait of Hormuz following the Iranian drone attack.
3.  **Iran's Hormuz Fee Proposal:** Iran proposed collecting up to $40 billion annually in fees for security, safety, and environmental services in the Strait of Hormuz, a plan rejected by the US and Oman.
4.  **Indefinite Israeli Occupation:** Israeli PM Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz declared that Israeli forces would remain indefinitely in "security zones" in Lebanon, Syria, and Gaza.
5.  **IDF-Hezbollah Engagements:** The IDF killed six Hezbollah operatives in southern Lebanon. Separately, an Israeli reserve soldier (Master Sgt. (res.) Basil Sweid, 32) was killed in an "operational accident" in Rab al-Thalathine, and four other soldiers were injured in Ya'aroun.
6.  **Damage to US Bahrain Base:** A Wall Street Journal investigation revealed that Iranian attacks caused extensive damage to the US Naval Support Activity Bahrain, with rebuilding costs estimated at $400 million, leading the Pentagon to review its regional force posture.
7.  **US-Iran Military Communication Channel:** US Vice President JD Vance reported an agreement to establish a direct military communication channel between Iran's IRGC and US CENTCOM in Doha.
8.  **Venezuela Earthquake Disaster:** A series of devastating earthquakes in Venezuela resulted in 164-235 deaths, 1,520-4,300 injuries, and potentially tens of thousands missing, prompting international humanitarian aid efforts.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran's drone attack on a commercial vessel and its proposed transit fees directly challenging international shipping and US/Omani positions on freedom of navigation. The Israeli-Lebanese border remains an active flashpoint; despite declared ceasefires, ongoing IDF operations against Hezbollah and Israeli leaders' assertions of indefinite occupation in "security zones" risk triggering a wider conflict, especially with Quds Force warnings for Israeli withdrawal. The new US-Iran memorandum of understanding (MoU) and proposed communication channels are fragile, with divergent interpretations of its terms, particularly regarding Iran's use of unfrozen assets and its "red line" demand for Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon, potentially undermining diplomatic progress. Regional stability is further threatened by militia activity in Iraq and Houthi threats against Israeli presence in Somaliland.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States** welcomed the US-Iran MoU but, along with **GCC** members, stressed the importance of confronting Iranian threats, including missiles, drones, and proxies. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio was in the Gulf, reinforcing opposition to any Hormuz transit fees and discussing the MoU. US SOUTHCOM mobilized significant aid for **Venezuela** following the earthquakes. The **Trump Administration** is reportedly urging OpenAI to delay its next AI model release over national security concerns and is forcing Polestar to stop US vehicle sales in 2027. **Oman** is caught between US and Iranian pressures regarding the Strait of Hormuz, rejecting transit fees while engaging in dialogue with Iran on the waterway's administration. **Italy's** Prime Minister Meloni denied direct military involvement in the war against Iran, confirming only technical and logistical support. Italy and **France** announced a new coalition to support **Lebanon** post-UNIFIL mandate. France also intercepted a Russian "shadow fleet" tanker near Sicily. **Canada** announced the reopening of its embassies in Iran and Venezuela. **Russia** reported downing 660 Ukrainian drones and expressed willingness to participate in a UNSC resolution on any final Iran-US agreement. **China** officially launched 10G internet and pledged full support and aid to Venezuela. **Turkey** is reportedly being considered for reentry into the F-35 program and a $700 million jet engine deal for its KAAN fighter by the Trump administration, while Israel is considering recognizing the Armenian Genocide, a move that would antagonize Turkey. The **United Nations** International Maritime Organization (IMO) suspended ship escort operations in the Strait of Hormuz due to the Iranian attack and mobilized aid for Venezuela. **FIFA** controversially approved the display of pride flags at the Iran-Egypt World Cup match in Seattle, despite protests from both countries.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Reporting included significant contradictions regarding an alleged **Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon**, with a US official claiming a partial withdrawal and imminent LAF deployment, which was immediately denied by both IDF and Lebanese sources. Similarly, accounts of the **Hashd al-Sha'abi ammunition depot explosion in Diyala, Iraq** varied, with the Ministry of Defense reporting an explosion without casualties, while the specific Hashd al-Sha'abi brigade involved denied any incident at its facilities. Estimates for **missing persons in Venezuela** following the earthquakes ranged wildly from 200 to over 50,000, indicating severe reporting gaps and potential for inflated figures.

Unverified claims include the **Iranian media's publication of a "rare" photograph** of Quds Force Commander Qaani and Supreme National Security Council Secretary Zolghadr, the specific context and rarity of which are not independently confirmed. **Iran's estimate of generating $40 billion annually** from Hormuz transit fees is also an unverified projection.

Propaganda indicators are present in several statements: **Iranian officials' declarations of a "great victory" over the US and the breaking of the "Israeli project"** align with narrative shaping efforts. Similarly, **Israeli leaders' firm statements about "indefinite occupation" of security zones** in neighboring countries serve to project strength and deterrence. One source, "omid dana امید دانا," displayed extreme anti-Hussein rhetoric ("لعنت بر حسین") alongside pro-Trump/Netanyahu views and speculation about a "next war," which is indicative of highly biased and potentially destabilizing content rather than objective analysis. **Yemen's Ansarullah leader Abdul-Malik al-Houthi's praise for Iran's "great victory"** also fits into a clear propaganda framework.

Reporting gaps primarily exist in the **specific details of the Singapore-flagged cargo ship attack**, including its exact name (referred to as *Ever Lovely* and *Ever Lonely*), the nature of the drone, and precise impact location beyond "near Oman." More specifics on the "pilot areas" for security arrangements in Lebanon negotiations and the exact implementation status of the proposed **US-Iran direct military communication channel in Doha** are also lacking.
